pr_title: GDScript: Fix setter being called in chains for shared types
pr_body:
When a type is shared (i.e. passed by reference) it doesn't need to be called in a setter chain (e.g. `a.b.c = 0`) since it will be updated in place.

This PR adds an instruction that jumps when the value is shared so it can be used to skip those cases and avoid redundant calls of setters. It also solves issues when assigning to sub-properties of read-only properties.

There are some duplicate issues for this that I could find:
Fixes #28720
Fixes #31245
Fixes #57793
Fixes #60796
pr_comments:
Unfortunately this seems to break access to types that are returned by value:
```gdscript
var dict : Dictionary = { "A":Transform2D() }
dict["A"].origin = Vector2(1.0, 2.0)
```
Has no effect

Same goes for:
```gdscript
var tr = Transform3D()
tr.basis.x = Vector3(2.0, 0.0, 0.0)
```

Edit: If this is intended behavior I think it needs a warning as it's quite straight forward and easy to miss

issue_context.title: [Godot4 Alpha1] setter called twice
issue_context.body:
### Godot version

v4.0.alpha1.official [31a7ddbf8]

### System information

Windows 10

### Issue description

![aaa](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/35988767/152951928-79767c63-98ce-4c7c-8c23-82bb27828c1e.PNG)
I only call 'editor=<sth>', but it's setter called twice.

### Steps to reproduce

Please run the reproduction project

### Minimal reproduction project

[GetSetTest.zip](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/files/8022196/GetSetTest.zip)
comments: I think that might be expected, your setter for `value` sets `editor.value`, which triggers a setter call for `editor`.

> And this bug was bring after Godot4 Alpha1

Do you mean that it worked fine in 4.0.alpha1 and no longer since? Your report says that you use Godot 4.0 alpha 1 so I'm confused.

@akien-mga, Sorry about my english was not good.
I mean, before 4.0alpha1, there was not this bug, since 4.0alpha1 there have this bug

It looks like the unexpected setter is called in the line `editor.value = val`. This doesn't only happen with inner-classes, and also happens with regular classes. Beyond this, it only happens when you change the property using the specific variable.

In this case, the double setter is called.
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/38119387/152972804-57fe32d6-f9de-4574-bd39-d23e67f20cc1.png)

In this case, using an intermediate variable, the double setter is avoided. The property change still takes effect, but the setter is not called.
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/38119387/152973302-698c5849-4f80-4af7-a0b5-9b1fc9edf745.png)

Ran into this this morning. Minimal reproduction:
```gdscript
extends Node

var test: Dictionary:
	set(value):
		test = value
		print("Setter called")

func _ready():
	test = {}
	test.b = 1
```
